transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's this cough that just won't go away. It's been waking me up at night and I'm getting a bit more puffed than usual.
Can you tell me when this cough first started and how it came on—what was going on at the time—and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
It's only been a few days, really. And no, I don't have any allergies to medicines that I know of.
Can you tell me how much this cough is affecting you, and what medicines you're taking right now—including any new or changed ones and, if you know, the doses?

It's disturbing my sleep most nights, I'd say about a 6 out of 10. For inhalers I use a blue salbutamol one — I'm needing it 4 or 5 times a day now instead of my usual twice — plus Fostair 100/6, two puffs twice a day, and lisinopril 10 mg once a day for my blood pressure.
Could you tell me about your past health—any ongoing health problems, past illnesses, operations or hospital stays—and where you feel this cough, and whether it moves or spreads anywhere?
I've had COPD for about 8 years now — that's the main long-term thing. The cough feels like it's in my chest, it doesn't really spread anywhere else.
Can you tell me what seems to make your cough better or worse—anything like activities, positions, foods, or medicines?
Cold air sets it off, and talking for a long time does too. Steam inhalation helps a little.
Is there anything else you've noticed besides the cough and feeling more puffed than usual?
I've been bringing up some white-to-yellow phlegm, more than my usual morning stuff. Other than that, no blood, no weight loss, no night sweats and no chest pain.
What worries you most about this cough?
I'm worried my lungs are getting worse, or that this could be something like cancer.
When you cough, what does it feel like?
It's a chesty cough — I bring up that white-to-yellow phlegm with it. It's worst in the morning and at night, and the fits can last a few minutes.

Besides the two inhalers and the lisinopril for your blood pressure, is there anything else you take — any other medicines, tablets, or things you buy yourself, including anything new or recently changed?
No, that's the lot — just the two inhalers and the lisinopril. I haven't started anything new or bought anything myself.
You've told me about your COPD — is there anything else about your past health, like other long-term conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays, that you'd like to add?
No, nothing else I can think of. Just the COPD, really.
Is there anything else you've noticed along with the cough that we haven't talked about yet?
Just that I get a bit more breathless than usual when I walk to the shop. Nothing else really.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
